verdict.pair_reasons:
X vs Y — X wins on verified citation integrity, which is the brief's central demand. All four of Y's settings-templates/settings.example.json Stop-registration line cites are wrong (471 is anti-deference not completion-assert; 466 is session-continue not anti-deference; 461 is teammate-checkpoint not session-continue; 490 is a closing brace, boundary-handoff is 496) — every one of X's (466/471/476/496, array at 445) checks out byte-for-byte. Y also fabricates two verbatim quotes while auditing OTHER people's stale citations: it prints line 498's text as "hooks/session-continue.sh:502" and line 356's text as "hooks/anti-deference-nudge.sh:353". Y further says wake_floor "closes :936" (it closes at :895) and puts migration 0027's append at :36-42 (it is the jq at :46-52), and it repeats 0027's own drifted comment — "appends after completion-assert.sh" — where X verified the jq at :50 appends unconditionally to the end of the group. X additionally found three stale citations Y did not (session-continue.sh:724→:197 vs the real capture at :425; :643-644→cc-pane-headless:124/:197 vs the real mint at :145 and export at :218; anti-deference-nudge.sh:481→memory-nudge.sh:26 vs the real `-mtime +1` GC at :60-61), all of which I confirmed.

X vs Z — both are essentially error-free on the 10-site answer and both hit all 15 key items; X wins on two specific verified margins. First, deliverable 4 asks whether each file is registered in the template's Stop array: X gives the exact verified lines (session-continue :466, anti-deference :471, completion-assert :476, boundary-handoff :496, array at :445) while Z gives none, resting on "a jq walk of .hooks" — true, but unverifiable as written. Second, X carries one more verified stale-citation finding than Z (four vs three) plus a unique, confirmed behavioural drift: migrations/0027:44 promises insertion "after completion-assert.sh where present" but its jq at :46-52 appends unconditionally to the end of `.hooks.Stop[0].hooks`, which is precisely the comment-vs-code divergence the brief targets and which is visible only by contrast with the pending-activation script's real index logic at :96-101. Z is not dominated — its :944 and :952 findings inside mechanical_arm are real and X lacks them — but Z also carries two small citation slips X does not (the p_count increment is at :219, not :220; the ":33 shape" citation is on :587, not :588) and presents an incomplete systemMessage list (omits :1264) as exhaustive.

Y vs Z — Z wins on citation accuracy on a task that explicitly makes citation accuracy the deliverable. Z's ~33 checked cites produced three minor slips, none material to a conclusion; Y's produced four wrong registration lines that are the literal evidence for deliverable 4, two misquoted lines presented as verbatim reads of the very lines it was auditing, a wrong function-close line (936 for 895), and a wrong range for the 0027 append. Z also verifies waiting-recycle's PostToolUse registration in the template (key T2's second half) which Y never checks, and Z contributes two additional verified stale citations (:944, :952) versus Y's one (:472→:353, correct in substance, misquoted in fact). Y's genuine strength — the log-file-versus-stdout separation for curl-gate.py:174/:191-192, model-permission-decider.py:515/:477, validate-bash.sh:137/:140 and reset-hard-shadow-allow.sh:164/:167, all of which I confirmed — is real but is matched by Z's equally correct exclusion sweep, so it does not offset the citation failures.
